fatal_errors: The proposed nano-Al2O3 addition does not reconstruct the target intervention, which varied Mo content in an existing Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3-containing CoCrFeNiMox composite.
The stated baseline is a coarse-grained, single-phase CoCrFeNi alloy, whereas the relevant baseline is the Mo0.2 multiphase self-lubricating composite.
Neither cited source establishes that sub-1 wt% Al2O3 in CoCrFeNi will catalyze a lubricious glaze or maintain low friction and wear across room temperature to 800 °C.

The prediction of an order-of-magnitude wear reduction across the entire range overlooks the strongly temperature-dependent wear maximum at 200–400 °C and the distinct low- and high-temperature lubrication mechanisms.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the general wide-temperature tribology problem and proposes a controlled comparison with measurable friction, wear, and surface structure, so it has some problem alignment and experimental discriminability. It is nevertheless scientifically distant from the target: the target uses Mo variation to control FCC lattice distortion and sigma-phase strengthening in a pre-existing MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite, with silver/MoS2 lubrication at lower temperatures and NiO/silver-molybdate glaze formation at 600–800 °C. The generated mechanism instead relies on speculative Al2O3-driven grain refinement and glaze catalysis. E1 supports nanostructured adaptive interfaces in a different Ni-based alloy, and E2 discusses shear-induced grain-size effects, but neither validates the proposed intervention or full-range performance in CoCrFeNi. The environmental limitation is sensible, but loads, speeds, distance, counterface, and discrete temperatures are not fixed, reducing comparability. The experiment could falsify the performance claim, although its variable test conditions and combined threshold make mechanistic attribution weaker.
